notes: Synthetic moat-validation case (Type C). useAuth's catch block swallows token-expiry errors and returns { user: undefined, error: undefined } — identical to the never-logged-in shape. The DOM renders 'Hello, Guest!' (legitimate logged-out UI) even though localStorage had a structurally-valid-but-expired token. Spec is correct (sets up an expired-token session, expects the user-name greeting; this would pass IF token refresh worked OR if the expired-state surfaced an error so the UI could prompt re-login). Snapshot-distinguishable: useAuth's hook state shows { user: undefined, error: undefined } vs the expected { user: undefined, error: 'TokenExpired' } — the absence of the expiry error in the captured hook state, combined with the localStorage having a token at all, is the fingerprint. From DOM alone the failure looks like 'user just isn't logged in' — many candidate hypotheses (login flow broken, MSW handler missing, race condition with bootstrap, token storage key mismatch, etc.). From the tree the diagnosis is: hook ran, found token, errored, but the error is gone — therefore the catch swallowed it. Patch target: in the catch block, set the error field to 'TokenExpired' so the caller can branch on error and render the re-login prompt. Pairs with case-022 (Type A: NaN fallback) and case-023 (Type B: sibling-state leak).
